**Self** — what a self is — the minimal, bodily and pre-reflective self, self-models and the sense of being a subject, the self as process or as context, and whether machines or groups can be selves. Not the person, which is personhood (group: philosophy; ADR-024).

| [CLAIM-196](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-196.md) | A person's roles in contexts that do not meet cannot contradict one another: role conflict needs an overlap, which segregating audiences prevents and collapsed contexts create | The MoM manuscript models a person's roles ("daughter", "teacher", "friend") as sections over family, professional and social contexts, with identity as their global section, failing when the roles contradict. Roles in contexts that do not meet glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)), so contradiction between them is not yet a failure. Conflict needs an overlap: an occasion on which two audiences are present at once. People manage the cover. They segregate audiences, which keeps the contexts disjoint, and they script the occasions where audiences must meet. Broadcast and networked media collapse contexts, which creates overlaps the person did not choose (boyd 2008, after Meyrowitz 1985). | Proposed |
| [CLAIM-198](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-198.md) | Preference reversal is not yet disunity: interests that govern a choice at disjoint times glue, and a self is divided over a choice only on an overlap, which the agent's prediction of its own later valuation creates | Take an agent's interests as sections over contexts of choice, each governing the windows of time in which its valuation ranks first. If the windows do not overlap, the sections glue ([CLAIM-197](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-197.md)): someone who prefers the diet in the morning and the cake at night is a time-indexed preference, not a divided self. Division needs an overlap, a choice on which both interests bear at once. On Ainslie's account that overlap is made by recursive self-prediction: the present choice is valued as a forecast of the later ones, so the later interest's valuation enters the present context. That is where intertemporal bargaining happens, and it is the coupling [CLAIM-163](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-163.md) found missing. | Proposed |

| [CLAIM-485](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-485.md) v2 | In the self-governing sense, what endogenous governance adds over a behaviourally equivalent system with an external scheduler is not that it allocates authority among its own processes but that it can revise its own governing standards when they break down | The bridge the owner asked for on 2026-10-28, between Kahl's proposal (THEORY-1165), which is about agency in the sense that bears on responsibility, and [QUESTION-092](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-092.md), which fixes [TERM-045](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-045.md)'s sense 5, self-governing. Internal allocation of authority, the second of [CLAIM-025](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-025.md)'s separable capacities (governing among regimes), coordinates execution and does not make a system govern itself more than an external scheduler would. | [CLAIM-491](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-491.md) v5 | No action is selfless in the sense of aiming at a good that is no self's: what is called selflessness, collectivist or altruistic, is concern for the good of a self extended to include others or a group, so collectivism is self-interest on a larger self-identity | The owner's position, from the discussion that raised self-categorization theory (2026-10-28 and 29). | [CLAIM-492](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-492.md) v2 | If the self is defined to include whatever an agent cares about, the claim that all motivation serves the self is true by definition and rules nothing out; the thesis has content only with a criterion of the self's extent that can come apart from what the agent cares about | The classic objection to psychological egoism (Butler; Sober and Wilson, [LIT-1683](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1683.md)), turned on the owner's thesis. "Every motive is my motive" is trivially true and does not make every motive self-interested. "My self includes whatever I care about" makes the thesis unfalsifiable. It is answered if the thesis names an independent criterion of the self's extent, such as overlap, fusion or salient self-categorization, and predicts that motivation follows that criterion and not caring alone. | Active |
